findings.text: DEVIATIONS.md says each deviation was logged before the data it concerns was read. D2 (20:50 UTC, 8c54acb9e2) lists the seeds found in 2201-2600 and was committed with that block, after the 1801-2200 block (d202be88ca). The extensions are the frozen rule and were announced in commit messages before their data; the stop of 2601-3000 cannot change the five smallest seeds (1..2600 fully covered). Its 'deleted unread' statement cannot be verified from git.

The IC walk's per-step mix64 hash and two coefficient additions mod r (genus_ladder.rs 1590-1594) and the large-prime table operations are not emitted, so 'fully charged' / 'every native operation is charged' is slightly overstated. Pricing 3 per walk step moves x* from 0.8759 to 0.8848 (p = 16411) and 0.6399 to 0.6457 (p = 32771) at w = 1; x at 16411 from 0.9987 to 1.0040. No D1 decision changes.

findings.topic: scope of 'below the ideal negation-rho bound at all w'
findings.text: Correct as stated for x* at both primes and x at 32771 (upper bound < 1 at w = 0, 0.1, 1). Scope: 5 prime-order genus-4 Jacobians per prime (#J about 2^56 and 2^60), 6 targets x 2 seeds each, counted group operations plus w per native operation; reference is the closed-form expected cost of an ideal random walk on the r/2 negation classes (a heuristic floor, not a measured walk and not a proven lower bound); by linearity the order holds for every w up to 1.142 (x*, 16411), 1.565 (x*, 32771), 1.300 (x, 32771). No wall-clock statement.

The theory cited is right (Gaudry 2000; Gaudry-Thome-Theriault-Diem 2007, O~(q^(2-2/g)); rho O~(q^(g/2))). 'What is new here' is a novelty statement not checked against the knowledge base (unavailable to producer and validator) and should be scoped to this lab's implementation. The crossing is at the pessimistic w = 1 end; at w = 0 and 0.1 the IC arm was already below the floor in the earlier study. The 'p^1.62 / p^1.54' figures are two-point local slopes between p and 2p, not exponent fits (AGENTS.md section 5 asks for at least four sizes); at w = 0 the slopes are 1.340 and 1.383.
'linear algebra from 77-81% of native work to 56-60%': the 56-60% are LA over total w = 1 cost (la_share_w1); over native work they are 76.7-80.8% and 56.2-60.6%.

cc* = 1.4 is at the lower edge of the grid {1.4, 2.0, 2.8}; the optimum is not located. The best cc = 2.0 cell costs 1.110x the choice, so the cc choice is robust; the SGE choice (4,1.5) over (8,2) at cc 1.4 is a 0.72% margin on 12 keys. 'The optimum falls with p' is consistent (p = 8209 chose the upper edge 2.0) but neither optimum is located.

analyze.py reseeds the same generator for both primes, and both have the same design, so replicate j uses the same index pattern at both primes: the D2 slope interval is not from independent per-prime bootstraps as PROTOCOL section 6 says. With an independent stream at 32771: x [-0.3847, -0.3699], x* [-0.4612, -0.4463] (claimed [-0.3841, -0.3706], [-0.4622, -0.4455]). The protocol does not fix the draw order; an interleaved order moves interval ends by at most about 2e-4. No decision changes.

No w_cal was measured for the mod-p and mod-r counters (owner rule 2026-11-12). Because the order holds up to the break-even w (1.14 or more), it holds at w_cal and 10 w_cal for any w_cal below 0.114 GAE per operation; one Jacobian group operation here is about 394 counted F_p multiplications and 7 inversions. 'Ranked at calibrated price' is an inference, not a measurement. Pricing mod-r operations like F_p operations is not material to the verdict: with F_p relation work at 1 GAE, x* reaches the floor only if a mod-r LA operation costs more than 1.25 GAE (16411) or 1.93 GAE (32771).

Bench record 20261118T1652Z-genus4-prime-order is still open (closed_utc null), raw entries not uploaded (no S3, disclosed), the 58 search files are not listed in it; its 8 raw hashes match the blobs and its 5 metrics match the recompute. The measured plain-rho sanity check (5 runs, 0.804x sqrt(pi r/2), per run 0.48-1.38) is noisy by design; no measured rho at p = 32771 (disclosed).
